candidates.source_title: Council completes £3.3 million purchase of Warwick Mill - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developer Kam Lei Fong. Once a thriving cotton mill, the imposing structure, which was built in 1907, has been vacant for at least a decade and has since become an eyesore, regularly attracting vandalism and urban explorers. The council sees redevelopment of Warwick Mill, which is Grade II listed, as a major opportunity to bring an important historic building back into use as new homes for the benefit of the Middleton community. The neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, has also been purchased as part of the £3.3 million deal, with plans to demolish the building. Work to transform the building will get under way quickly. Rochdale firm Winterburns is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, including 1,000 tyres and overgrown plants and trees. Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year. The council will then kick start the process of tendering a developer partner to undertake the longer-term work of bringing Warwick Mill back into use.

candidates.source_title: McCann's encouraging message to 'top class' Grehan after Rochdale error
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers has backed defender Sean Grehan to grow into a ‘top-class’ footballer and has given the youngster plenty of words of encouragement. Grehan has established himself as a regular starter this season after being a slightly more peripheral figure at times last term. However, the Republic of Ireland Under-21 captain, who played the full 90 minutes of Rovers’ 6-1 loss to MK Dons, was substituted at half-time during the 4-1 win over Rochdale after a clumsy error which allowed veteran Ian Henderson to open the scoring after 15 minutes. “Sean's top. He's going to be top-class,” McCann told the Free Press. “He's 21 years of age.I said to him after the game, ‘I don't ever want you to stop making those types of passes. I want you to keep that sort of bravery about you.’ “He's made a mistake because he tried to break a line with a pass.I'm OK with that. I'm fine. We're all human at the end of the day.We make mistakes.” “If I said that to my centre-halves, we wouldn't have seen the pass from Jay McGrath for the second goal or the unbelievable split in the lines with passes. I want my centre-backs to be brave. “So, he'll probably do it again. Hopefully it doesn't lead to a goal against us. And Jay will do it and Byrne will do it and Matty will do it. But I want them to be brave. And that's the most important thing.” McCann also explained that the decision to take off Grehan at half-time had always been in his mind heading into the Rochdale match due to the amount of minutes that the defender has played recently. He said: “With Sean, I just said, ‘look, don't be down because of that. Do it again. Make sure you're better with your execution the next time.’ “We're always going to make substitutions at half-time. Sean was always in the head, particularly after playing the whole game on a Saturday. So, it was more of a rotational game, really, the Rochdale game.”

candidates.source_title: National Pathology Week: Meet the team behind millions of tests every year
candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week marks National Pathology Week, a chance to celebrate the often unseen workforce whose expertise underpins modern healthcare and supports almost every patient journey. Our pathology teams process more than 10 million samples and perform over 35 million tests every year, supporting patients across Greater Manchester and beyond. While patients may never meet the professionals working in pathology laboratories, their role is critical. In fact, around 95% of clinical pathways rely on pathology services, providing the diagnostic information clinicians need to diagnose illness, guide treatment and monitor ongoing care. At the heart of this work colleagues are combining scientific expertise with the latest technology to deliver faster, more efficient testing for patients. Earlier this year, the Oldham laboratory introduced new automated biopsy processing technology designed to support specimen preparation around the clock. The system can operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, helping improve workflow, create additional capacity and enable biomedical scientists to spend more time on highly specialised diagnostic work. The introduction of the technology builds on a wider programme of innovation within the laboratory, which has also led the way in adopting digital pathology, allowing specialists to review biopsy samples digitally and collaborate more easily across healthcare organisations. The past year has also seen colleagues successfully implement a new Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) across pathology services. The major programme has transformed how laboratories manage samples and results, with teams across all sites working together to ensure services for patients continued uninterrupted throughout the transition. The NCA's pathology workforce includes almost 700 colleagues working across Oldham, Salford, Rochdale, Bury, Wigan, Wrightington and Leigh. Together they represent a diverse range of professions including biomedical scientists, pathologists, clinical scientists, mortuary practitioners, biomedical support workers, transfusion practitioners, microbiologists, virologists, biochemists, point of care testing teams, administrators, porters and messengers.

candidates.source_title: Resident escapes from second floor as fire tears through sheltered housing flat
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Fire crews rushed to a sheltered housing residence in Middleton this evening (November 5) after a blaze broke out at a second-storey flat. Eyewitness reported seeing fire engines and police parked on Sedgley Street and Nelson Street, responding to a fire that had broken out at Lonsdale Court. The building provides sheltered housing to the over-60s and is managed by Rochdale Borough Council. Three fire engines rushed to the scene where the building and neighbouring flats were evacuated. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The fire service said that one resident 'self-rescued' from the property before they arrived and that safety checks were ongoing now that the fire was extinguished. A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said, “Just before 7pm this evening (Thursday, 5 th November), firefighters were called to reports of a fire at a supported living residence on Nelson Street in Middleton. “Three fire engines from Chadderton , Blackley and Heywood fire stations quickly arrived at the scene, where a flat on the second floor of the building was alight. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on this dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism - the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body's functions. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. candidates.source_title: Man, 38, threatened two police officers with kitchen knife in Heywood - The Bury Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who threatened two police officers with a kitchen knife in Heywood has been given a hospital order. Samuel Penrose, 38, of Partington Street, Castleton, was convicted of four knife-related offences following an incident on West Starkey Street on April 26. The court record states that Penrose threatened a police officer with a kitchen knife in a public place in a way that would cause a reasonable person to believe there was an immediate risk of physical harm. He was also convicted of possessing the kitchen knife without good reason or lawful authority in a public place. Penrose further threatened a second police officer with the knife in a public place before threatening the same officer with the weapon at a private address on West Starkey Street. He indicated guilty pleas to all four offences on April 27 and was convicted on the same date. The case was dealt with at Manchester Crown Court on Friday, October 30. The court imposed a hospital order, under which Penrose will be admitted to or detained at Prestwich Hospital.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An Asda worker has been praised for her kindness after going above and beyond to support a recently widowed customer. Saheda Bibi, 43, has worked at Asda in Rochdale since 2012. After learning that a customer had lost her husband, Saheda promised the woman's daughter that she would look after her mum. The daughter, who lives in London, was worried about how her mum would cope on her own. Saheda reassured her by explaining which days she worked, allowing the customer to plan her shopping trips around her shifts. Since then, Saheda has helped the woman with her shopping, scanning and packing her items, making sure she has a chair to sit on and finding time for a friendly chat. The customer was so grateful for the support that she contacted store customer manager Dave Jeffs to share her appreciation. Dave has since nominated Saheda for an Asda Service Superstar Award.

candidates.source_title: 'Terrific at times' - Cliff Byrne's assessment of Doncaster Rovers' performance against Rochdale - Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: It was Jersey Mike’s delight for Doncaster Rovers, who came back from behind to secure a thumping 4-1 victory away at Rochdale. There was nine changes made from the team that were hammered by MK Dons on Saturday, with Brandon Hanlan marking his return to the starting lineup with his first goal this season, in an evening which also saw Alfie May, Owen Bailey and Isaac Hutchinson all add to their tallies for the season. Cliff Byrne said: “At the start, we wanted to secure our place in the next round. I think the level of the performance tonight was terrific at times. It was exhilarating. I know we didn’t have many fans in the stadium tonight but the ones that were here I think will appreciate that.” Rovers came from behind to secure the victory, marking the first time the team has managed that across all competitions since beating Rotherham United on derby day back in February. Sean Grehan was at fault for Rochdale’s opener in a challenging evening for the young defender, who was replaced by Owen Bailey at half-time. He added: “We did conceded from an error and our behalf and we got punished for it. I think over the course of the game we had a lot of control and we showed in particular during the second-half a lot of calmness in the top end of the pitch, which resulted in the four goals.” Reflecting on his team’s spirit along with the first-half error, Byrne added: “We ask the players to play a particular way and we give them autonomy within that to be flexible within the guidelines of how we like to play. Sometimes mistakes can happen and it’s important that we don’t be overly critical because we want players to take opportunites and we want them to be risk takers as well. “It’s important that the whole group contribute and I think we’ve seen that tonight.”

candidates.source_title: 'Played with intent', 'A true captain's performance': Doncaster Rovers player ratings from EFL Trophy win at Rochdale - Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers came from behind to secure a well-deserved 4-1 victory away at Rochdale, securing their place in the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy in the process. Grant McCann made nine changes from the team that was thrashed away at MK Dons on Saturday. Josh Clarke was selected in goal, Jay McGrath and Tom Nixon returned to the defence while there was also opportunities for the likes of Harry Clifton, Darren Robinson, Bayley McCann and Brandon Hanlan among others. Jack Senior and Sean Grehan were the only players to keep their place in the starting lineup. Doncaster Rovers got off to a challenging start and were forced into an early change after just three minutes when new arrival Will Keane was forced off with an injury. Hanlan could and probably should have put Rovers in the driving seat moments later, but was denied by a strong save by Sam Waller. Matters got worse after 15 minutes when the hosts took an early lead, latching on to a mistake from Sean Grehan, which allowed Ian Henderson to easily tap home from close-range on his record-breaking 532nd appearance for the Dale. McCann’s men made more changes at the break, introducing both Owen Bailey and Jordan Thomas in an effort to rejuvenate their hopes of progressing to the next stage of the competition and it very much worked the trick. Rovers levelled proceedings in the 54th minute through Alfie May’s close distance strike after great work from Clifton in the build-up. The Vikings then the took the lead nine minutes later when Hanlan netted his first of the season from close range after some brilliant work by both McGrath and Thomas. Bailey, who was brought on to play centre-back in the second half, put the game to bed with a close-range finish in the 88th minute, capping off a true captain’s performance from the 27-year-old. Subsitute Isaac Hutchinson then topped off a great day for the visitors with a goal from close distance. Here are our player ratings from Doncaster Rovers’ final EFL Trophy group stage game.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A derelict factory in Rochdale was once the world’s largest producer of asbestos – a toxic material which has led to the death of thousands in the UK. Now the owner of the old Turner Brothers factory in Spotland will carry out investigations to locate where the asbestos has been buried. Spodden Park Ltd, who own the 75-acre site, say the asbestos won’t be disturbed during the work. The contractor carrying out the works will provide a better understanding of the landscape so when the site clean up does happen, it can be done safely. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. A spokesperson for Spodden Park said: “Over the next few weeks, a specialist contractor will undertake investigation works across the site. These investigations will enable us to better understand ground conditions across the site, including the location of asbestos beneath the ground. Baillie Street Quarter won the new Best Art in the Community award for outstanding artwork from the recent Common Walls International Mural Festival, organised by talented local artist Hayley Garner. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Just over a month on from the High Court battle over Hopwood Hall, the door has been left open for reconciliation. Hopwood DePree, an American filmmaker who wanted to buy the historic landmark from Rochdale Council, had entered an option agreement with the council to restore the hall back in 2017, until that agreement was terminated by the council in October 2024. Since then, Mr DePree, who claims ancestral connections with the 1400s stately home, has felt he had a legally binding agreement to purchase Hopwood Hall for £1. However, in September, following a two-day trial in Manchester Civil Justice Centre, the court ruled that the council was not acting unlawfully when it ended the exclusivity agreement with the American filmmaker. Therefore, Mr DePree’s claim was lost. Now, the filmmaker has issued an open letter to town hall bosses to set out his terms for a resolution discussion. This comes after council leader Neil Emmott told the latest town hall meeting his ‘door is always open’ to Mr DePree. He added that if Mr DePree came back with a viable plan for the future of Hopwood Hall, the council would listen. Both sides have said a costly court battle could have been avoided. But Mr DePree’s latest open letter to the local authority suggested it was the council that took ‘an incredibly aggressive legal route of termination and locking them out of Hopwood Hall’. The council has always maintained that the volunteer group was barred due to safety reasons. The reasons for the ending of the agreement by the council and being booted out of the hall are still something Mr DePree says he doesn’t understand. The US-born adopted Middletonian wants to see the council release documents about communications between authorities about how they handled dealings about the hall; commission an independent review; correct inaccurate public statements about his community-led effort; and to pause further action in the ongoing legal proceedings and enter into discussions to find an amicable solution. In his letter, he said: “I hope we can find an amicable resolution for Hopwood Hall. At the October 15, 2026 public council meeting, you stated that your ‘door is always open’ and ‘Rochdale council is willing to listen’ if I come forward with a sustainable plan, following the council’s unexpected termination of our community-led rescue in 2024. “I would welcome constructive discussions but they must begin with a clear explanation of why our previous proposal was rejected. Nearly two years after our heritage team was locked out, the council still has not provided meaningful answers and continues to refuse to release documents and communications about decisions taken. “Despite our challenges, I remain open to constructive dialogue, including an independently moderated public forum where councillors, volunteers and residents can address concerns and explore Hopwood Hall’s future. “Given the time-sensitive nature of our legal options, we must reserve our rights. candidates.source_title: Jimmy McNulty pips Pep to top manager award - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Former Rochdale AFC boss Jimmy McNulty has been crowned manager of the season for guiding Rochdale back into the football league. Although McNulty announced his departure for Stockport County following The Dale’s promotion to League Two, he was shortlisted for the award alongside former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, Michael Carrick at Manchester United and Steven Schumacher at Bolton Wanderers. And last night he scooped the top honour at the at the North West Football Awards. Rochdale AFC celebrated: “Jimmy McNulty has been crowned Manager of the Season at the North West Football Awards after guiding Rochdale back into the Football League. A well deserved recognition! 👏🏆” The Dale were nominated in three other categories. Liverpool FC Women beat Rochdale the to the Best Club Fan Engagement honour, with Carlisle United Football Club, and Salford City Football Club also in the running. Stockport County Community Trust’s County Pals (Parkinson’s Active Lifestyle Support) won the Community Initiative of the Season, ahead of Rochdale AFC Community Trust’s Changing Lives FC initiative, Blackburn Rovers Community Trust for its Women’s Wellbeing Champions; Bolton Wanderers in the Community’s ASPIRE programme; and Fleetwood Town Community Trust-s Go Beyond — Fleetwood Community Hub. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Find out the latest events from November 4 from All Across the Arts columnist Steve Cooke Rochdale’s streets will be transformed into an immersive night-time light and audio experience this winter, as the excellent Stories We Tell: Rochdale invites you to explore the borough through the real memories, voices and lived experiences of local people. This guided audio walk will use large-scale projections, moving imagery and powerful 3D sound to animate buildings and streets across the town centre, including Milkstone Road and Rochdale Town Hall Square. Audiences will journey through Rochdale after dark, encountering stories of belonging, change and hope gathered directly from local communities. “Stories We Tell is a powerful way to honour our past, celebrate the present and keep the stories of our community alive,” said Hayley Garner, street mural artist who contributed to the project. This is an outdoor guided walk; you are asked to please dress for the weather and wear appropriate footwear. The route begins at Rochdale Train Station and ends at Rochdale Town Hall. The route is flat and mostly follows a path but there are some road crossing moments - don’t worry, volunteers are on hand to support every step of the way.
